outcome: Since 26 January 2024 the symmetric case has been re-proved for n = 3 (Chen, Li, Xi and Xu, May 2026, a case settled in 2017/2020), and on 6 October 2026 OpenAI released a preprint in its openai/math repository (family 087) claiming the symmetric inequality vol(K)·vol(K°) ≥ 4^n/n! with equality characterised by Hanner bodies in every dimension, plus a general-body claim and a symplectic-width claim; as of 13 October 2026 I found no named qualified human who has checked the argument, the only formal evidence is a Lean development whose repository manifest reads 'status: unchecked' at top level, and the claim is unrefereed.
problem_asks: Part (1): for every dimension n (the bullet states no range; the conjecture is for all n), and every centrally symmetric convex body K in R^n with polar K° = {y : <x,y> ≤ 1 for all x in K}, the product vol(K)·vol(K°) is at least 4^n/n!. Part (2): the conjecture's minimum is attained at the cube and its polar, the cross-polytope (and more generally at Hanner polytopes, as the conjectured minimisers). The bullet's wording ('the product of the volumes') does not itself spell out equality, so I have listed the equality characterisation as part of what the conjecture predicts, and recorded it separately. Not asked by this bullet: the non-symmetric version (general convex bodies with the simplex as minimiser), the functional or log-concave versions, and local minimality of Hanner polytopes.

events.what_happened: Mahler's planar case: the volume-product inequality for centrally symmetric planar convex bodies, in 'Ein Minimalproblem für konvexe Polygone' (Mathematica (Zutphen) B, 1939). Cited as a solved case in the Wikipedia article 'Mahler volume' (last edited 7 October 2026). Some search snippets give 1938; the Wikipedia citation gives 1939. I did not open the primary paper.
events.delivers: Proves the symmetric inequality |K|·|K°| ≥ 4^n/n! for n = 2, all centrally symmetric planar convex bodies. Restricted to dimension 2.
events.remains: All n ≥ 3 for the symmetric inequality, and the equality characterisation for n ≥ 3.
events.direction: Confirms the conjectured lower bound (cube/cross-polytope) for n = 2.

events.what_happened: Saint-Raymond (1980) confirmed the symmetric conjecture for unconditional convex bodies (invariant under reflections in the coordinate hyperplanes). Cited on the Wikipedia 'Mahler volume' article. I did not open the primary paper, and I did not establish the journal.
events.delivers: Symmetric inequality for all n, restricted to unconditional bodies.
events.remains: Symmetric bodies that are not unconditional, for every n ≥ 2; the equality characterisation beyond the unconditional class.
events.direction: Confirms the conjectured bound within a class containing the cube and cross-polytope.

events.what_happened: Meyer (Israel J. Math., 1986) gave a shorter proof of the unconditional case, and Meyer with Reisner characterised equality for it. Cited on the Wikipedia 'Mahler volume' article; the primary paper was not opened, and the equality attribution is from search summaries.
events.delivers: A shorter proof of the symmetric inequality for unconditional bodies, plus equality characterisation in that class.
events.remains: Same as the Saint-Raymond entry: non-unconditional symmetric bodies, n ≥ 2.
events.doubts: Primary not opened; the equality attribution comes from search summaries of the Wikipedia citation list.
events.direction: Confirms the conjectured bound within the unconditional class.

events.what_happened: Bourgain and Milman showed that the symmetric volume product is at least c^n·4^n/n! for some constant c, so the conjecture holds up to an exponential factor. Cited in the arXiv 1303.4197 abstract text and in the Kuperberg page. I did not find a source giving the year in what I read; I believe it is 1987 but have not confirmed it.
events.delivers: Asymptotic lower bound, exponential-in-n accuracy only: a bound of the form c^n·4^n/n! with unspecified c.
events.remains: The exact conjectured constant for every n.
events.doubts: The year is not confirmed in any source I read; it is my own recollection.
events.direction: Partial: a bound off by an exponential factor, in the direction of the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Kuperberg, 'From the Mahler conjecture to Gauss linking integrals' (arXiv v1 30 Oct 2006; Geom. Funct. Anal. 18 (2008) 870-892). The abstract page I opened says the paper proves a version of the bottleneck conjecture that gives a partial solution of the Mahler conjecture. The explicit constant π/4 (so a lower bound π^n/n!) is from the 1303.4197 text and from secondary summaries; I did not see that inequality in the abstract text I could read.
events.revisions: v2 14 Dec 2006; v3 2 Jul 2008 adds an extension to the asymmetric case.
events.delivers: A partial lower bound for symmetric bodies, of the form (π/4)^n times the conjectured value (π^n/n! in total), by way of a bottleneck-type statement. Not the exact bound.
events.remains: The exact bound 4^n/n! for every n.
events.doubts: The constant π/4 is not in the abstract text I read; it comes from a search snippet of arXiv 1303.4197 and from secondary summaries.
events.direction: Partial: a bound in the direction of the conjecture, off by (π/4)^n.

events.what_happened: Artstein-Avidan, Karasev and Ostrover, 'From symplectic measurements to the Mahler conjecture' (arXiv v1 18 Mar 2013; Duke Math. J. 163 (2014) 2003-2022). Links Viterbo's symplectic isoperimetric-type conjecture to the symmetric Mahler conjecture: if the Hofer-Zehnder capacity of convex domains of fixed volume is maximised by the ball, then a hypercube minimises the volume product among centrally symmetric bodies. A reduction, not a resolution.
events.delivers: A conditional reduction: the symmetric bound follows from a Viterbo-type capacity-maximality statement for convex domains. It settles nothing on its own.
events.remains: The symmetric conjecture itself, unless the symplectic hypothesis is established. Whether the hypothesis is affected by the 2024 Viterbo counterexample (see haim-kislev-ostrover-2024-05) is not established by any source I read.

checked_by.who: Duke Mathematical Journal (refereed, journal of record)

events.direction: Conditional reduction in the direction of the conjecture (cube as minimiser).

events.what_happened: Karasev, 'Mahler's conjecture for some hyperplane sections' (arXiv v1 24 Feb 2019; Israel J. Math. 241 (2021) 795-815). Uses symplectic techniques to confirm the symmetric conjecture for hyperplane sections or projections of ℓ_p-balls and for Hanner polytopes.
events.delivers: The symmetric inequality for a restricted family: hyperplane sections or projections of ℓ_p-balls, and Hanner polytopes. Not all symmetric bodies.
events.remains: Symmetric bodies outside those classes, for every n.

checked_by.who: Israel Journal of Mathematics (refereed, journal of record)

events.direction: Partial, in the direction of the conjecture, on a restricted class.

events.what_happened: Kim, 'Minimal volume product near Hanner polytopes' (arXiv 1212.2544, December 2012). Shows each Hanner polytope is a strict local minimiser of the volume product in the symmetric class under the Banach-Mazur distance; the journal version is J. Funct. Anal. (2014) per Wikipedia. Opened only through search snippets; the abstract was not opened.
events.delivers: Local minimality of Hanner polytopes among symmetric bodies. Local, not global; does not settle the conjecture.
events.remains: The global symmetric inequality; the local statement is neighbouring to the conjecture's equality cases.
events.doubts: Not opened; the description is from search snippets and the Wikipedia citation list.
events.direction: Neighbouring to the equality cases: local minimality of the conjectured minimisers.

events.what_happened: Iriyeh and Shibata, 'Symmetric Mahler's conjecture for the volume product in the three dimensional case' (arXiv v1 6 June 2017; Duke Math. J. 169(6) (2020) 1077-1134). Proves the symmetric inequality for n = 3, with the equality characterisation. The arXiv version is 60 pages. The Chen et al. preprint attributes to this paper a bound of 32/3 with equality for affine images of the cube or octahedron (body or polar a parallelepiped), per the search summaries.
events.revisions: v2 25 Oct 2017; v3 10 Jul 2019; journal version Duke 2020.
events.delivers: The symmetric inequality for n = 3, with equality characterised. Restricted to dimension 3.
events.remains: n ≥ 4 for the symmetric inequality, and n = 2 is already settled by Mahler.

checked_by.who: Duke Mathematical Journal (refereed, journal of record)
Fradelizi, Hubard, Meyer, Roldán-Pensado and Zvavitch
checked_by.qualification: Established specialists in convex geometry and the volume product; Meyer is an author of the unconditional-case result.
checked_by.what_they_did: Published a shorter, self-contained proof of this n = 3 result along the same lines (see fradelizi-et-al-2019).

events.direction: Confirms the conjectured bound for n = 3 and the conjectured equality cases.

events.what_happened: Fradelizi, Hubard, Meyer, Roldán-Pensado and Zvavitch, 'Equipartitions and Mahler volumes of symmetric convex bodies' (arXiv v1 24 Apr 2019; v4 20 Jan 2021; Amer. J. Math. 144(5) (2022), per search summaries). A short proof of the n = 3 symmetric case, following Iriyeh and Shibata's two key steps (an equipartition theorem refining Hadwiger's, and a volume-product inequality), plus an alternative equality proof and a stability result.
events.delivers: A self-contained proof of the symmetric inequality for n = 3, with alternative equality proof and a stability statement. The authors note the ideas cover a large family of convex sets in every dimension.
events.remains: The general-n symmetric inequality. The family in every dimension is restricted and is not stated as a resolution.

checked_by.who: American Journal of Mathematics (refereed, journal of record)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published in Amer. J. Math. 144(5) (Oct 2022), per search summaries; the journal page was not opened.

events.direction: Confirms the conjectured bound for n = 3, a second proof.

events.what_happened: Fradelizi and Marín Sola, 'Entropy, slicing problem and functional Mahler's conjecture' (arXiv 2406.07406, June 2024). Carries Klartag's convex-body slicing results over to log-concave functions and relates a strong functional slicing conjecture to the functional Mahler conjecture. Not opened; described from search summaries.
events.delivers: Relates functional slicing and entropy to the functional Mahler conjecture for log-concave functions. Not about convex bodies, so it does not move the bullet's quantity.
events.remains: The bullet's convex-body conjecture, untouched.
events.doubts: Not opened; described from search summaries only.
events.direction: Neighbouring: a functional analogue of the volume product; does not cut either way on the bullet.

events.what_happened: Mastrantonis and Rubinstein, 'Two-dimensional Błocki, L^p-Mahler, and Bourgain conjectures' (arXiv v1 19 Jan 2024; v2 12 Jul 2024). Confirms Błocki's Bergman-kernel conjectures in dimension two and a broader L^p-Mahler family, where p = ∞ gives the classical Mahler conjectures, in dimension two only. Predates the frozen revision (26 January 2024), so it is outside the window.
events.delivers: In dimension two only: confirms a broader L^p-Mahler family whose p = ∞ case is the classical Mahler inequality. Two-dimensional, so it does not reach n ≥ 3.
events.remains: All n ≥ 3 for the symmetric classical case.
events.direction: Dimension-two results in the direction of the conjecture; outside the window.

events.what_happened: Haim-Kislev and Ostrover, 'A Counterexample to Viterbo's Conjecture' (arXiv v1 26 May 2024; Annals of Mathematics 203(2) (2026), online 1 March 2026 per search results). Disproves Viterbo's volume-capacity conjecture for convex domains in every dimension n ≥ 2, so the symplectic capacities do not coincide on convex domains. This is a neighbouring symplectic result, not a statement about the volume product. I opened the abstract page only; the explicit counterexample bodies were not visible in what I read.
events.revisions: v2 and v3 exist (arxiv.org/html/2405.16513v2, v3 in search results; not opened).
events.delivers: Disproves Viterbo's volume-capacity conjecture for convex domains in R^{2n}, n ≥ 2. It does not decide the volume-product conjecture.
events.remains: The symmetric and general Mahler conjectures are not settled by this event. Whether its counterexample bodies are of the form K × K° relevant to the Artstein-Avidan–Karasev–Ostrover reduction is not established by my sources.

checked_by.who: Annals of Mathematics (refereed, journal of record)
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted and published in Annals of Math. 203(2), 2026, per search results (journal page not opened).

events.doubts: Not established whether the counterexample's Lagrangian products are of the type K × K° that the Mahler reduction and the Family 087 symplectic claim use. I did not read the bodies in the paper.
events.direction: Neighbouring: falsifies the symplectic conjecture that the Artstein-Avidan–Karasev–Ostrover reduction is built on; direction for the Mahler bullet is not determined.
events.object: Haim-Kislev and Ostrover exhibit a counterexample to Viterbo's volume-capacity conjecture in every dimension n ≥ 2 (Minkowski billiard dynamics, per search summary). The explicit bodies were not read.

events.what_happened: Iriyeh and Shibata, 'Minimal volume product of three dimensional convex bodies invariant under certain groups of order four' (arXiv v1 25 Sep 2024; v2 1 Oct 2024; 35 pages). Gives the sharp lower bound of the volume product of three-dimensional convex bodies invariant under two kinds of discrete subgroups of O(3) of order four, and characterises the minimisers; states that this gives partial results on the non-symmetric version in dimension three.
events.delivers: Sharp bound and minimisers for the volume product of 3D bodies invariant under two classes of order-four groups. Non-symmetric in general, but restricted to these invariance classes; the bullet's symmetric problem is not covered.
events.remains: The symmetric conjecture for all n, and the general non-symmetric conjecture.
events.direction: Neighbouring: different (non-symmetric) question on restricted classes; cuts in the direction of the conjectured minimal product for those classes.

events.what_happened: Fradelizi and Nakhle, 'The functional Mahler conjecture for even s-concave functions' (arXiv 2412.12372, December 2024). Sharp forms of the functional Mahler conjecture for even s-concave functions in dimensions 1 and 2. Not opened; described from search summaries.
events.delivers: Functional versions in dimensions 1 and 2 for even s-concave functions. Not the convex-body quantity.
events.remains: The bullet's convex-body conjecture.
events.doubts: Not opened; described from search summaries only.
events.direction: Neighbouring functional analogue; does not cut on the bullet.

events.what_happened: Gilboa, Segal and Slomka, 'The Scaled Polarity transform and related inequalities' (arXiv 2502.11524, February 2025). Rescales the polarity transform so that the induced Mahler-type product has upper and lower bounds with the same asymptotics. Not opened; described from search summaries.
events.delivers: A rescaled polarity transform with two-sided bounds of the same asymptotic order; a different transform, so not the volume product of the bullet.
events.remains: The bullet's exact conjecture.
events.doubts: Not opened; described from search summaries only.
events.direction: Neighbouring; does not cut on the bullet.

events.what_happened: Aliev, 'Mahler-type volume inequality for convex bodies with tetrahedral symmetry' (arXiv 2511.14991, 19 Nov 2025, one version). Proves |K|·|(K−K)°| ≥ 3/2 for planar K (a new proof), and for three-dimensional bodies with tetrahedral symmetry |K|·|(K−K)°| ≥ 2/3, equality for the tetrahedron. The quantity is the polar of the difference body K−K, not K's own polar.
events.delivers: Difference-body polar bounds in dimension 2 (new proof) and for 3D bodies with tetrahedral symmetry. Different quantity and restricted symmetry class.
events.remains: The bullet's volume product for centrally symmetric bodies, in every dimension.
events.doubts: Only the abstract page was read; the introduction, which would state the status of the symmetric conjecture in each dimension, was not visible.
events.direction: Neighbouring: a different quantity (K−K and its polar) and a restricted class; does not cut on the bullet.

events.what_happened: Jiménez Cuevas, 'A Discrete KKT Variational Characterization of the Local Minimality of the Mahler Volume in Centrally Symmetric Polytopes' (arXiv v1 10 Apr 2026; v2 16 Jun 2026 'matches the version under peer review' per its comment; v3 6 Aug 2026). Claims the Hanner orbit is a strict and topologically isolated local minimum of the Mahler volume in the space of centrally symmetric polytopes modulo GL(n).
events.revisions: v2 16 Jun 2026 revised the local minimality theorem and truncation lemma; v3 6 Aug 2026.
events.delivers: A local statement: Hanner polytopes are strict local minimisers among symmetric polytopes modulo GL(n). Local, polytopal, and modulo linear maps; it does not establish the global minimum.
events.remains: The global symmetric inequality for all bodies and all n.
events.doubts: The author's comment says the version is under peer review; I could not confirm submission or acceptance. I read only the abstract and metadata, not the proof.
events.direction: Neighbouring: local minimality of the conjectured minimisers, within polytopes; cuts in the direction of the conjectured minimisers, locally.

events.what_happened: Chen, Li, Xi and Xu, arXiv 2605.09334, first posted 10 May 2026 under the title 'The Non-Symmetric Mahler Conjecture in Dimension Three' (v1); v2 20 May 2026; v3 15 June 2026 retitled 'The Mahler Conjecture in Three Dimensions', merging an earlier symmetric-case paper. The abstract says the method 'solves the conjecture for general convex bodies in three dimensions by developing a method called the shadow flow', gives the sharp bound |K||K°| ≥ 64/9 (equality for simplices with centroid at the origin, Santaló-point polar), and gives a new proof of the three-dimensional symmetric case first proved by Iriyeh and Shibata. Seminar talks by the authors took place in May and June 2026 (PKU 20 May, Westlake, HUST 10 June, CCNU), which are presentations of the same preprint and are not separate events.
events.revisions: v2 20 May 2026; v3 15 June 2026 (title changed from 'The Non-Symmetric Mahler Conjecture in Dimension Three' to 'The Mahler Conjecture in Three Dimensions'; merges the symmetric paper 2605.13795).
events.delivers: Symmetric: a new proof for n = 3 only, of the bound already proved by Iriyeh–Shibata (32/3), stated as a reproof with equality characterised as affine images of cube or octahedron (Theorem 7.1 attributed to Iriyeh–Shibata). Non-symmetric (not this bullet's question): sharp bound 64/9 for every convex body in R^3 with the Santaló-point polar, simplices as equality. Nothing for n ≥ 4.
events.remains: Symmetric inequality for all n ≥ 4. Non-symmetric general-n conjecture. The bullet's n = 3 symmetric case was already settled before this event.
events.doubts: Version history is inconsistent: v1's title and content differ from v3, and the v3 comment says the symmetric paper 'will not be submitted separately', while arXiv 2605.13795 was posted separately on 13 May 2026. I read the v3 HTML through a summarising fetch, and v1 and v2 were not read. No independent public check of the three-dimensional argument was found.
events.direction: For the symmetric bullet: confirms the conjectured minimum for n = 3 by a new proof, consistent with the conjecture, and adds nothing for n ≥ 4. For the non-symmetric question: a claimed sharp bound at n = 3 in the direction of the general conjecture.

events.what_happened: Chen, Li, Xi and Xu, 'The Symmetric Mahler Inequality in Dimension Three via Admissible Shadow Systems', arXiv 2605.13795, posted 13 May 2026 (one version). Gives a purely geometric proof, via symmetric admissible shadow systems, of the three-dimensional symmetric inequality |K||K°| ≥ 32/3, crediting Iriyeh–Shibata and Fradelizi et al. with the earlier proofs.
events.delivers: A new proof for n = 3 only, of the symmetric inequality already proved by Iriyeh–Shibata and Fradelizi et al.; no new dimension.
events.remains: Symmetric inequality for all n ≥ 4.
events.doubts: Single-version preprint; I read the abstract page only. The authors' affiliation list includes Shanghai University (Xi) and USTC (Chen, Xu), and no public check of the argument was found.
events.direction: Confirms the conjectured minimum for n = 3 by a new proof; no change for n ≥ 4.

events.what_happened: Guberman, 'A connection between the Mahler conjecture and floating bodies' (arXiv 2608.10994, 11 Aug 2026, one version). The abstract says it proves a result about polytopes whose floating bodies are not smooth, which is then used to prove a result about the combinatorial structure of minimisers of the volume product. I read only the abstract page.
events.delivers: Per the abstract only: a structure statement for polytopes with non-smooth floating bodies, and a consequence about the combinatorial structure of volume-product minimisers. It does not state a new value of the infimum or a symmetric-case bound in the abstract I read.
events.remains: The value of the minimum, and the symmetric inequality for all n, as far as the abstract shows.
events.doubts: Scope (symmetric or not, which dimensions) is not visible in the abstract, and the full text was not read.
events.direction: Neighbouring: structural information about minimisers; direction on the bullet not determined from the abstract.

events.what_happened: OpenAI released a batch of mathematical manuscripts from 'an internal OpenAI model' on 6 October 2026 in the public repository github.com/openai/math (Apache-2.0 per the repository page), reported as 722 manuscripts in 372 families; the README now counts 719 after three withdrawals. Family 087, titled in the Lean docs 'The Mahler conjectures, functional inequalities and polar-product symplectic width', comprises three preprints whose file names carry the date 22 September 2026: 'The symmetric Mahler conjecture and its equality cases', 'The Mahler Conjecture for General Convex Bodies', and 'Symplectic Balls in Symmetric Polar Products'. The claims, as I read them from the Lean docs and manifest and from secondary coverage: (a) symmetric: for every n ≥ 1, every compact convex symmetric K in R^n with nonempty interior has vol(K)·vol(coordinatePolar K) ≥ 4^n/n!; (b) equality holds iff K is an invertible linear image of a Hanner body (Lean: symmetric_mahler_equality, IsLinearHanner); (c) general: for compact convex bodies with nonempty interior, the infimum over interior z of |K|·|(K−z)°| is at least (n+1)^(n+1)/(n!)^2, with simplices as equality cases (per the scope page and Kingy; the file GeneralMahler.lean was not located); (d) symplectic: for n ≥ 2 and symmetric K, the Gromov width of int K × int K° is 4, and every ball of capacity 0 < c < 4 embeds symplectically (Lean: symmetric_polar_main; the scope page says an embedding at capacity exactly 4 is not asserted). Secondary coverage (Kienzle blog, Kingy, Kalai) reads the symplectic step as constructing a ball of radius 2/√π, which has capacity 4. The volume bound follows from (d) by letting c tend to 4, so the sup statement suffices for (a). The release is not peer reviewed; the repository's own text says results are 'at different stages of verification'.
events.revisions: The three preprint file names carry 22 September 2026, but the first public commit is 'Initial commit' on 6 October 2026, so I date the event to 6 October. Commit 'Update manuscripts and Lean formalizations' on 8 October 2026 changed the repository; I could not see its diff. history.md (7 October 2026) records 14 manuscripts revised with proof repairs and 13 updated citations, and names three withdrawn Hodge-type papers; it does not name family 087, but the 14 revised items are not listed in what I read.
events.delivers: As claimed (not verified by me or by any named expert): the symmetric inequality 4^n/n! for every n ≥ 1 for all centrally symmetric convex bodies, with equality exactly for linear images of Hanner bodies, and the general-body infimum bound with simplex equality (scope and Lean statement of the general file not confirmed); plus a symplectic capacity claim for K × K°. Full coverage of the bullet's question (symmetric inequality for all n, and equality), as claimed.
events.remains: Nothing of the bullet, as claimed. Unverified points: the imported Lean lemmas and definitions (coordinatePolar, IsLinearHanner, gromovWidth, HasSymplecticEmbedding) were not read; the general-body Lean file was not located; the paper's own argument (PDF) was not readable; no journal or expert verification.
events.time_since_posted: 7 days as of 13 Oct 2026; only informal reactions: Kalai's blog (7 Oct) says verification is pending, and a blog by Elliot Kienzle (Oct 2026) explicitly says 'I haven't checked the line-by-line details (which is important, because this paper doesn't come with a Lean proof)'. Neither claims verification.

machine_checked.system: Lean (openai/math lean/OAI project, with Comparator configs), pinned at commit adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a
machine_checked.notes: No 'sorry', 'admit', 'axiom' or 'native_decide' in the three declaration files I read (OAI/Analysis/Mahler/MainTheorem.lean, Classification.lean, OAI/Geometry/PolarProducts/Main.lean). Their imports (HomogeneousEndpoint, HomogeneousMassAssembly, Splitting, UpperBound) and the lemmas they cite were not read, so sorry-freedom of the whole dependency closure is unverified. The formalization.yaml top-level block reads 'status: unchecked' and 'scope: Partial progress.', and it has no per-entry review field I could read. The general-body Lean file (GeneralMahler.lean, cited by the scope page) was not found in the manifest or the directories I opened, and the lean/docs/087.md links returned 404 for the file names it gives.

events.doubts: (1) Not peer reviewed, and no named qualified mathematician has publicly worked through the argument; the Kalai post and the Kienzle post both disclaim checking, and the repository says 'Some of the unformalized results could have issues'. (2) The Lean files I read state the claims, but the definitions of coordinatePolar, IsLinearHanner, gromovWidth and HasSymplecticEmbedding (and the imported lemmas) were not read, so I cannot say the formal statements match the English conjecture. Kalai warned that 'even Lean verification may have issues'. (3) Kienzle reports the paper itself 'doesn't come with a Lean proof'; the Lean code is in a separate folder. (4) The scope page is internally inconsistent: an early passage says 'The nonsymmetric Mahler conjecture and the functional inequalities are not included', and a later passage supplies the general-body theorem. The general-body bound is printed with an ambiguous comma between |K| and |(K−z)°|. (5) The scope page says an embedding at capacity exactly 4 is not asserted, while the Kienzle blog says the proof constructs a ball of radius 2/√π (capacity 4); the volume bound needs only the supremum, so this is a difference of content to be settled, not a fatal one. (6) The symplectic step relies on symplectic-capacity claims about K × K°, in the same family as Viterbo's conjecture, which Haim-Kislev and Ostrover disproved in 2024. I found no source saying whether the disproof touches this class, and the Mahler-Viterbo link (Artstein-Avidan–Karasev–Ostrover) is conditional. (7) The 14 revised manuscripts are not listed in what I read, so I cannot rule out a revision to family 087. (8) Accounts of verification coverage disagree across secondary sources (about 42%, 63% and 22% Lean-formalised), and none gives coverage for family 087 specifically. (9) An OpenAI spokesperson's statement that results are 'not yet fully understood even by the company's own mathematicians' appears only in a search summary.
events.direction: Cuts in favour of the conjecture as stated: it asserts the conjectured lower bound 4^n/n! for every n for symmetric bodies, with equality for Hanner bodies (the conjectured minimisers), and the simplex as the general-body minimiser. It does not assert a counterexample. Whether the claims are correct is not established by my sources.
events.object: No counterexample. Two constructions are claimed. (i) A characterisation of the equality cases for symmetric bodies as linear images of Hanner bodies, built from intervals by Cartesian products and convex-hull joins (per the Lean file docstring/definition summary). (ii) For each symmetric convex body K in R^n, n ≥ 2, a symplectic embedding into int K × int K° of every ball of capacity c < 4 (Gromov width 4), where the blog says the construction is of a ball of radius 2/√π. Whether these are explicit or non-constructive was not visible from the Lean statements I read; the Kienzle blog describes the symplectic step as an AI-made construction.

systems.name: an internal OpenAI model
systems.what_it_did: Per the repository README, the manuscripts and proof artifacts (including family 087) were 'produced by' the model. The README does not name it. Secondary coverage describes the model producing the mathematical arguments of family 087, including the symplectic embedding (Kienzle blog) and the equality classification (Kalai, Kingy). I did not read the paper's own account of the model's role, because its PDF was not readable.
systems.basis_quote: contains mathematical manuscripts and supporting proof artifacts produced by an internal OpenAI model

ai.disclosed_cost: The README says: 'On average, each result used three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute with that model.' This is a batch-level average, not a figure for family 087. Kingy notes no dollar, token, accelerator-hour or training-budget totals are disclosed.

disputes.summary: Chen, Li, Xi and Xu posted a sharp three-dimensional bound of 64/9 for general convex bodies on 10 May 2026 (arXiv 2605.09334). OpenAI's family 087 (released 6 October 2026) claims the general bound (n+1)^(n+1)/(n!)^2 in every dimension, which agrees with 64/9 at n = 3. No source I read sets out a formal priority claim. An informal blog (Kienzle, Oct 2026) says its author has been 'scooped' by the AI proof of the general case. The disputed item is the general (non-symmetric) bullet, not the symmetric one this record covers.

summary: Sources. I ran 39 searches (listed below) and opened 46 of the 58 sources in the sources array; the OpenAI preprint PDFs were unreadable, so for family 087 I read the Lean files that the scope page and manifest point to. The main findings are these. (1) The symmetric conjecture is settled for n = 1 and n = 2 by Mahler (1939), for unconditional bodies by Saint-Raymond (1980) and Meyer (1986), and for n = 3 by Iriyeh and Shibata (arXiv June 2017, Duke 2020), with Fradelizi, Hubard, Meyer, Roldán-Pensado and Zvavitch giving a shorter n = 3 proof (arXiv 2019, Amer. J. Math. 2022). Karasev (2019) covers hyperplane sections of ℓ_p-balls and Hanner polytopes; Kuperberg (2006/2008) gives a bound off by (π/4)^n. (2) In the window, the only events bearing on the symmetric bullet are: Chen, Li, Xi and Xu (arXiv 2605.09334 and 2605.13795, May 2026), which re-prove the n = 3 symmetric case and claim a non-symmetric three-dimensional result; and OpenAI's family 087 (repository released 6 October 2026). Several other in-window items are neighbouring, not the bullet's quantity: Iriyeh–Shibata (restricted non-symmetric classes, Sept 2024), Haim-Kislev–Ostrover (Viterbo counterexample, May 2024), Aliev (difference body, Nov 2025), Jiménez Cuevas (local minimality among polytopes, Apr 2026), Guberman (floating bodies, Aug 2026), and functional analogues by Fradelizi and co-authors, Gilboa–Segal–Slomka and others. The 2024 Haim-Kislev–Ostrover paper is important for the OpenAI route; see below. (3) The OpenAI claim. Read from primary text: the repository README and the Lean files (opened at a pinned commit) state the Lean theorems I summarise in the event; this is a reading of what is stated, not a check that the statements are correct. The symmetric statement is for all n ≥ 1 with the bound 4^n/n! and equality characterised by linear images of Hanner bodies; the symplectic statement is Gromov width 4 for int K × int K° in n ≥ 2 (with 'capacity exactly 4 not asserted'). The Lean statements were read, but the definitions and imported lemmas were not, and the sorry status of the import closure is unverified. The manifest's top-level review status reads 'unchecked'. Not verified: the paper's own argument (the PDFs are binary to my tools); who, if anyone, has checked it (no named qualified mathematician has publicly claimed to verify it; Kalai's blog and Kienzle's blog both disclaim checking); whether the 14 revised manuscripts include family 087; and the general-body Lean file (not located). Secondary coverage gives a symplectic route through a ball of radius 2/√π and reports the blog-level description of the construction; I did not verify those descriptions against the paper. (4) Close calls. (a) Whether the OpenAI claim 'settles' the bullet: as claimed, yes, for all n and both the inequality and the equality classification; as checked, no. I record it as an unverified claim of the bullet's full question, not as a settled status. (b) Whether the Haim-Kislev–Ostrover counterexample touches the class K × K° used in the family's symplectic step: not established. The Artstein-Avidan–Karasev–Ostrover hypothesis (Hofer–Zehnder capacity maximised by the ball at fixed volume) is close in form to the Viterbo-type statement that was disproved, but from the abstract I could not establish whether the disproof covers the specific capacity they use; I record it as an open question for the later pass. (c) Whether the Chen et al. 2026 result counts for the bullet: its symmetric part is a re-proof for n = 3 only, so it moves nothing for the bullet's question beyond the earlier n = 3 result. Its non-symmetric part is a different question. (d) Whether the 22 September 2026 date on the preprint folders is the first public written argument: I dated the event to 6 October 2026, the first public commit, since I found no earlier public posting. (e) The AI attribution: OpenAI's README says the manuscripts were 'produced by an internal OpenAI model'. That is the lab's own account, but it is not specific to family 087 and it is not the paper's own sentence, which I could not read. I record the system as 'an internal OpenAI model' and do not date or name it. The 'Astra' model OpenAI announced on 1 August 2026 is not the same announcement: the August list of ten results does not include the Mahler conjecture (DataCamp summary), and I found no source linking Astra to the October batch. (5) Other AI searches: no AI involvement is recorded for any of the other Mahler-related events. The 2026 Chen et al. preprints have no AI sentence in the text I read, and none of the older papers names a system.
competing_reading: The strongest case for the OpenAI claim: the symmetric statement is a Lean-stated theorem for all n ≥ 1 with the conjectured constant and an equality classification, and the statements look like the conjecture. If the Lean definitions match the standard definitions (polar, volume, the Hanner class), the bullet's quantity is settled for every n by a machine-checked argument, and the 'unchecked' manifest flag is only bookkeeping. On this reading, the record should count the bullet as settled by an AI system in October 2026, with the verification status noted. The strongest case against: no qualified human has publicly checked the argument; the Lean definitions and the imported lemmas were not checked by me; the paper's own text is not readable; the symplectic route depends on a capacity statement in the family of statements that Haim-Kislev and Ostrover disproved for Viterbo's conjecture; the scope page is inconsistent about whether the general result is included; and the repository's own README says some unformalised results 'could have issues'. On this reading, the bullet's status rests on an unrefereed, partly unread claim, and should be recorded as claimed rather than settled.
what_would_settle_it: (1) Public, specific engagement from a convex geometer able to judge the argument: for example Iriyeh or Shibata, Fradelizi, Meyer, Reisner, Karasev, Ostrover, Kalai or Kuperberg, stating whether the proof of the symmetric inequality for general n is correct. (2) A Lean audit of the definitions (coordinatePolar, IsLinearHanner, gromovWidth, HasSymplecticEmbedding) and an 'axioms' check on the full import closure at a fixed commit, showing it is sorry-free and axiom-clean. (3) The authors' own PDF text, showing the argument, the model's role and any acknowledgement, which I could not read. (4) The repository's history for family 087 (the diff of the 8 October commit and the list of the 14 revised manuscripts), to show whether the Mahler preprints changed after 6 October. (5) Resolution of the scope page's contradictions (the 'nonsymmetric not included' passage; the general-body inf and comma; the capacity-4 wording). (6) An explicit statement from the symplectic-capacity side (Haim-Kislev, Ostrover or Balitskiy and co-authors) on whether the 2024 counterexample's bodies intersect the class K × K° used for the Gromov-width-4 claim. (7) Journal submission and acceptance, or a rejection, of the OpenAI preprints or the Chen et al. 2026 preprints. (8) For the bullet itself, a convex-geometry survey or a Wikipedia update after 7 October 2026 that either cites the OpenAI claim as settled or explains why it is not.

dead_ends: The OpenAI primary announcement (openai.com/index/sharing-ai-progress-in-mathematics/) returned HTTP 403 to the fetch tool. Secondary sources were used instead.

The OpenAI preprint PDFs (both Mahler preprints, the symplectic preprint and the reasoning trace) are served as binary PDF; the tool could not extract text. The paper's own sentences on AI, acknowledgements and authorship are therefore unread.

The Lean files named in lean/docs/087.md (MahlerConjecture.lean, SymmetricPolar.lean, GeneralMahler.lean) returned 404 at that path. The real paths were found in formalization.yaml: OAI/Analysis/Mahler/MainTheorem.lean, OAI/Analysis/Mahler/Classification.lean and OAI/Geometry/PolarProducts/Main.lean. The general-body file was not found in the manifest or the folders I opened.
The searches for 'Symplectic Balls in Symmetric Polar Products' and the family-087 title on the open web returned no paper; only the repository and secondary blogs carry them.
Quanta Magazine: no article on the Mahler conjecture found in search.

Search for a reaction from Iriyeh, Shibata, Fradelizi, Meyer, Reisner, Karasev, Ostrover or Kuperberg to the October claim: none found in the indexed sources. A later search that asked for October 2026 news on the symmetric Mahler proof returned no OpenAI coverage at all, though other searches did; the search index is inconsistent on this point.

A search for AI involvement in other Mahler-related preprints (AlphaEvolve, Claude, GPT-5, Gemini, AlphaProof) found nothing for the convex-body conjecture. The Claude-acknowledged 2026 'Mahler measure' paper (arXiv 2608.00615) concerns Boyd's Mahler measure, a different problem.
Aug 2026 OpenAI batch (ten results, including Ehrhart's volume conjecture) does not include the Mahler conjecture (DataCamp list), so it is not an event for this bullet.

The arXiv 2603.12495 (Balitskiy, Mitrofanov, Polyanskii) on Viterbo's inequality for planar K × Q: found in search only, not opened; it is about Viterbo's inequality in the plane, not the volume product.
